notes.text: Yet — They cover all their wickedness with a profession of religion. Delight - There are many men who take some pleasure in knowing God's will and word, and yet do not conform their lives to it. As - As if they were a righteous people. Forsook - As if they were not guilty of any apostacy from God, or disobedience to God's precepts. Ask - As if they resolved to observe them. In approaching - In coming to my temple to hear my word, and to offer sacrifices.

Afflicted — Defrauded our appetites with fasting, of which this phrase is used, Levit xvi, 29. Ye find - Either you indulge yourselves in sensuality, as they did, chap. xxii, 13. But this does not agree with that afflicting of their souls which they now professed, and which God acknowledges; or you pursue and satisfy your own desires: though you abstain from bodily food, you do not mortify your sinful inclinations. Exact - Your money, got by your labour, and lent to others, either for their need or your own advantage, which you require either with usury, or at least with rigor, when either the general law of charity, or God's particular law, commanded the release, or at least the forbearance of them.

Behold — Your fasting days, wherein you ought in a special manner to implore the mercy of God, and to shew compassion to men, you employ in injuring or quarrelling with your brethren, your servants or debtors, or in contriving mischief against them. Heard - In strife and debate. By way of ostentation.

Chosen — Approve of, accept, or delight in, by a metonymy, because we delight in what we freely chuse. For a day - This may be understood, either for a man to take a certain time to afflict his soul in, and that either from even to even, Lev. xxiii, 32, or from morning to evening, or for a little time. Wilt thou call - Canst thou suppose it to be so? A fast - It being such an one as has nothing in it, but the dumb signs of a fast, nothing of deep humiliation appearing in it, or, real reformation proceeding from it. Acceptable day - A day that God will approve of.
The bands — The cruel obligations of usury and oppression.

Cast out — And thereby become wanderers, having no abiding place. To thy house - That thou be hospitable, and make thy house a shelter to them that have none of their own left. Hide not - That seek no occasion to excuse thyself. Thy own flesh - Some confine this to our own kindred; but we can look on no man, but there we contemplate our own flesh, and therefore it is barbarous, not only to tear, but not to love and succor him. Therefore feed him as thou wouldest feed thyself, or be fed; shelter him as thou wouldest shelter thyself, or be sheltered; clothe him as thou wouldest clothe thyself, or be clothed; if in any of these respects thou wert in his circumstances.

Thy light — Happiness and prosperity. Break forth - It shall not only appear, but break forth, dart itself forth, notwithstanding all difficulties, as the sun breaks, and pierces through a cloud. Thy health - Another metaphor to express the same thing. Righteousness - The reward of thy righteousness. Before thee - As the morning-star goes before the sun. The glory - His glorious power and providence. Thy rereward - Thus the angel of his presence secured the Israelites when they came up out of Egypt.

Answer — He will give an effectual demonstration, that he hears thee. Here l am - A phrase that notes a person to be ready at hand to help. Take away - From among you. The yoke - All those pressures and grievances before mentioned. Putting forth - Done by way of scoff, or disdainful insulting. Vanity - Any kind of evil words.

Draw out — Or, open, as when we open a store, to satisfy the wants of the needy. Thy soul - Thy affection, thy pity and compassion. Thy darkness - In the very darkness of the affliction itself thou shalt have comfort.

Guide thee — Like a shepherd. And he adds continually to shew that his conduct and blessing shall not be momentary, or of a short continuance, but all along as it was to Israel in the wilderness. Satisfy - Thou shalt have plenty, when others are in scarcity. Make fat - This may be spoken in opposition to the sad effects of famine, whereby the flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen, and the bones that were not seen, stick out. A garden - If thou relieve the poor, thou shalt never be poor, but as a well-watered garden, always flourishing. Fail not - Hebrew. deceive not, a metaphor which farther notes also the continuance of this flourishing state, which will not be like a land-flood, or brooks, that will soon be dried up with drought. Thou shalt be fed with a spring of blessing, that will never fail.

They shall be of thee — Thy posterity. Waste places - Cities which have lain long waste; that shall continue for many generations to come. The breach - Breach is put for breaches, which was made by God's judgment breaking in upon them in suffering the walls of their towns and cities to be demolished. Paths - Those paths that led from city to city, which being now laid desolate, and uninhabited, were grown over with grass, and weeds. To dwell in - These accommodations being recovered, their ancient cities might be fit to be re-inhabited.

glossa.text:
*Cry.* ((HIER.)) The Lord to the prophets or to the apostles: the former chapter being ended, in which peace is announced to the just, and no rest to the wicked.

*As a trumpet.* ((ID.)) Where to the apostles, etc., *as far as* so let Israel, dead by sin, hear his own crimes.

*To my people.* As if he said: Let them see what a Father they have lost, who calls even sinners his people.

*As.* That is, why should I not hear them as I hear those who do justice in the Church, living justly and piously, confessing Christ true God and true man.

*They ask.* ((ID.)) Another rashness of the Jews, as though, trusting in a good conscience, they demand a just judgment, according to that: *Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence.*

*Why have we fasted.* They have forgotten the ancient history, that the Lord had no regard to the gifts of Cain, because he did not divide rightly with his brother, to whom he grudged charity towards God.

*Behold, in the day.* A fast acceptable to God is to abstain not only from foods, but from all unlawful things.

*You exact.* He who exacts from one who has not, does violence to God.
*Do not fast as until this day.* Lest he seem to reprove fasting, he teaches how one ought to fast.
*Is this such a fast.*
*The bundles.* ((ID.)) We understand sins, etc., *as far as* despise not the household of thy own seed.

*Break thy bread to the hungry.* ((ID.)) We break bread to the hungry, etc., *as far as* but the fullness of the soul.

*And thy own flesh.* ((ID.)) Recognize thy neighbour, in whatever need, as like to thyself, considering that thou art mortal and passible.

*Thy light.* As the morning light dissolves the darkness, so the light of truth puts errors to flight.

 *Justice.* Christ, who justifies all, shall go before unto glory.

*And the glory of the Lord shall gather thee up,* that is, shall receive thee to himself, who said: *Where I am, there also shall my minister be ((Joan. XII))*.
*To stretch out the finger.* To mark thy neighbours, to disparage them. That is, not only art thou not to think these things and not to do them, but thou art not even to disparage.

*A watered garden,* the paradise of delight, which the Lord God had planted from the beginning, namely the Church. The fountain in the midst is Christ, whose waters of spiritual doctrine do not fail, which water the Church. And this is, *And he shall be as a watered garden* , O faithful one, or O Church.

*As a fountain.* Thou shalt be made like to Christ, thy head.

*They shall be built* ((HIER.)) The Jews refer this to the restoration which was made under Zorobabel and Jesus the high priest; or to that which they rave will come at the last. Better may these things be referred to the Church.

*The foundations* ((ID.)) The apostles, the prophets and the like: Whence, *The foundations thereof are in the holy mountains ((Psal. LXXXVI))*. But the foundation in the singular number is Christ, whence, *Other foundation no man can lay, but that which is laid, which is Christ Jesus ((I Cor. III))*.

*Of iniquities,* otherwise *into rest,* namely the paths of error into rest or into true peace.

notes.text: Generation — The posterity.
Righteousness — The fruit or reward of his righteousness, which is God's blessing upon his estate.
Darkness — In the troubles and calamities of life. He - The upright man.

Lendeth — Gives freely to some, and lends to others according to the variety of their conditions. Affairs - His domestick affairs. Discretion - Not getting his estate unjustly, nor casting it away prodigally, nor yet withholding it from such as need it.
Moved — Though he may for a season be afflicted, yet he shall not be eternally destroyed.
Evil tidings — At the report of approaching calamities.

Dispersed — His goods, freely and liberally. Righteousness - His liberality, or the reward of it. Ever - What he gives is not lost, but indeed is the only part of his estate, which will abide with him to all eternity.

The desire — Either of the misery of good men; or of his own constant prosperity. We are here exhorted to praise God, ver. 1-3. Particularly for his glory and greatness, ver. 4, 5 And for his grace and goodness, ver. 6-9.

glossa.text: *Blessed is the man.* ((CASS.)) Here the Psalmist shows, after the deliverance, etc., *as far as* thirdly he affirms that adverse things befall the ungodly. *That feareth the Lord.* The fear of the world makes men wretched, but the fear of God makes a man desire those things whereby he is blessed. *In the commandments.* This the fear of God does, that he should will. And he says not "he shall do," etc., *as far as* and *the earthly habitation presseth down the mind that museth upon many things.*

*Mighty.* ((AUG., CASS.)) Behold the rewards of that blessed man. *His seed.* That is, the reward of a good work; *Shall be mighty upon earth,* not upon this earth, where he is a laughing-stock, but upon the heavenly. Or even here in this present time, wherein it is less seen. *Seed,* the works of mercy, whence comes the everlasting harvest. *Mighty,* because with a very small thing, even as with a great one, the kingdom of heaven is bought. *The generation.* Not of the flesh, but of imitation. Or the works of the upright. *The upright* are they who resist not the Father when he corrects, and who believe him when he promises, and who believe not that their works have perished when no requital is made them in time. For there are those who do those good things while hoping here for a reward from God, or wishing to please men, which is not the blessed man: and yet,

*Glory and wealth in his house.* That is, in the secret of the heart, where he dwells with the hope of eternal life, where holy riches and eternal glory are laid up. *Justice.* This is his glory, these are his riches, which nevertheless he has from God. *It remaineth for ever.* As it were, he is not blessed for a time.
*There hath risen up.* ((CASS.)) Secondly he treats of the coming of the Lord, etc., *as far as* that he may fortify it beforehand with firm allegations and assertions in the judgment. Or,
*He sheweth mercy.* ((ID.)) He who gives to the needy; *He lendeth,* he who grants a loan, to receive afterwards as much again.

*His heart is ready to hope in the Lord, his heart is strengthened, it remaineth,* etc. ((AUG.)) It is plain therefore that this man seeks not his own things, but the things which are Christ's; he bears labours patiently, he awaits the promises with confidence. ((CASS.)) Or, if any man threatens evils, he fears not, but is ready.

*He hath distributed.* He hopes not to fear, because he has distributed. *He hath given to the poor.* ((AUG.)) Behold, this man was buying what he did not see, but that other was keeping a treasure for him in heaven, who vouchsafes to hunger and to thirst in the poor upon earth. *His justice remaineth for ever and ever.* ((CASS.)) He gave what was his own, and lived justly and godly; or, he who gives what is his own works justice. *His horn shall be exalted in glory.* Because he is humble here, there he shall have power.

*The sinner shall see.* ((ID.)) Thirdly he affirms that contrary things befall the ungodly. By the good things of the blessed he exhorts, by the evils of the enemies he terrifies, and this psalm is an instructor of the faithful.

*He shall be angry, he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away, the desire of the wicked shall perish,* saying: *What hath pride profited us, and the boasting of riches? ((Sap. V))*

notes.text: And I accordingly came to you, not with loftiness of speech or of wisdom — I did not affect either deep wisdom or eloquence. Declaring the testimony of God - What God gave me to testify concerning his Son.

I determined not to know anything — To wave all my other knowledge, and not to preach anything, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified - That is, what he did, suffered, taught. A part is put for the whole.
And I was with you — At my first entrance. In weakness - Of body, 2 Cor. xii, 7 And in fear - Lest I should offend any. And in much trembling - The emotion of my mind affecting my very body.

And my speech in private, as well as my public preaching, was not with the persuasive words of human wisdom, such as the wise men of the world use; but with the demonstration of the Spirit and of power — With that powerful kind of demonstration, which flows from the Holy Spirit; which works on the conscience with the most convincing light, and the most persuasive evidence.
That your faith might not be built on the wisdom or power of man, but on the wisdom and power of God.

Yet we speak wisdom — Yea, the truest and most excellent wisdom. Among the perfect - Adult, experienced Christians. By wisdom here he seems to mean, not the whole Christian doctrine, but the most sublime and abstruse parts of it. But not the wisdom admired and taught by the men of this world, nor of the rulers of this world, Jewish or heathen, that come to nought - Both they and their wisdom, and the world itself.

But we speak the mysterious wisdom of God, which was hidden for many ages from all the world, and is still hidden even from "babes in Christ;" much more from all unbelievers. Which God ordained before the world — So far is this from coming to nought, like worldly wisdom. For our glory - Arising from the glory of our Lord, and then to be revealed when all worldly glory vanishes.

Had they known it — That wisdom. They would not have crucified - Punished as a slave. The Lord of glory - The giving Christ this august title, peculiar to the great Jehovah, plainly shows him to be the supreme God. In like manner the Father is styled, "the Father of glory," Eph. i, 17; and the Holy Ghost, "the Spirit of glory," 1 Pet. iv, 14. The application of this title to all the three, shows that the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost are "the God of glory;" as the only true God is called, Psalm xxix, 3, and Acts vii, 2.

But this ignorance of theirs fulfils what is written concerning the blessings of the Messiah's kingdom. No natural man hath either seen, heard, or known, the things which God hath prepared, saith the prophet, for them that love him. Isaiah lxiv, 4

But God hath revealed — Yea, and "freely given," ver. 12. Them to us - Even inconceivable peace, and joy unspeakable. By his Spirit - Who intimately and fully knows them. For the Spirit searcheth even the deep things of God - Be they ever so hidden and mysterious; the depths both of his nature and his kingdom.

For what man knoweth the things of a man — All the inmost recesses of his mind; although men are all of one nature, and so may the more easily know one another. So the things of God knoweth no one but the Spirit - Who, consequently, is God.
Now we have received, not the spirit of the world — This spirit is not properly received; for the men of the world always had it. But Christians receive the Spirit of God, which before they had not.

Which also we speak — As well as know. In words taught by the Holy Spirit - Such are all the words of scripture. How high a regard ought we, then, to retain for them! Explaining spiritual things by spiritual words; or, adapting spiritual words to spiritual things - Being taught of the Spirit to express the things of the Spirit.

But the natural man — That is, every man who hath not the Spirit; who has no other way of obtaining knowledge, but by his senses and natural understanding. Receiveth not - Does not understand or conceive. The things of the Spirit - The things revealed by the Spirit of God, whether relating to his nature or his kingdom. For they are foolishness to him - He is so far from understanding, that he utterly despises, them Neither can he know them - As he has not the will, so neither has he the power. Because they are spiritually discerned - They can only be discerned by the aid of that Spirit, and by those spiritual senses, which he has not.

But the spiritual man — He that hath the Spirit. Discerneth all the things of God whereof we have been speaking. Yet he himself is discerned by no man - No natural men. They neither understand what he is, nor what he says.
Who — What natural man. We - Spiritual men; apostles in particular. Have - Know, understand. The mind of Christ - Concerning the whole plan of gospel salvation. Isaiah xl, 13

glossa.text: *For I judged not myself to know anything.* He who speaks higher things to one less capable works not profit, but the display of himself.
*The perfect.* Not those who already know and are teachers, who have no need of it, but hearers now capable.

*In a mystery.* By expounding the mysteries of the Old Testament in which Christ was signified, as in the sacrifice of Abel, or of Abraham. *Which is hidden.* Because it is not in words, but in power: not comprehensible by human reason, but credible by the efficacy of the Spirit.
*For if they had known.* Either the lesser, that he was the Messiah promised in the law, or the greater, that he was God, or the Son of God: *they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.*

*Nor into the heart of man.* Below the heart of man is that which ascends into the heart; above the heart is that eternal thing to which the heart ascends. Or it is not man, but the spirit, that knows. *Hath ascended.* A thing is said to ascend in the heart when, being well understood, it pleases.

*Searcheth,* etc. The Spirit of God is said to search all things, not that he may find what he does not know, but because he leaves nothing at all that he does not know, or because he makes thee search; for what thou doest by his gift, he is said to do, because without him thou wouldst not do it.

*But the Spirit that is of God.* The Holy Spirit is assuredly of the Father and of the Son, and ours as well. For what has been given is referred both to him who gave, and to those to whom he gave. And so the Holy Spirit is not only of the Father and of the Son, who gave, but is also ours, who received. And this is not that spirit of ours in which we are: because that very spirit of ours in which we are is itself the spirit of man, which is in him. And yet we have received that very spirit also which is man's. But one thing is what we receive, that we might be, another what we received, that we might be holy. But the spirit of man is taken in Scripture for the soul itself, or for the rational power of the soul itself. For he gave us nature that we might be, a soul that we might live, a mind that we might understand. *That we may know.* Many have the gifts of God, and by not knowing from whom they have them, they are puffed up with impious vanity. No one is blessed by the gifts of God who is ungrateful to the giver, whence in the Gospel: *He that hath, to him shall be given.* To have fully is to know whence one has it. *He therefore that hath not,* that is, he who knows not whence he has it, *even that which he hath shall be taken away from him ((Luc. VIII))* .
*Spiritual things.* Which you Corinthians are not; and therefore it is your fault, not ours, that we have not spoken greater things.

*But the sensual man.* A man is called sensual in respect of life, who is carried along by the dissolute wantonness of his own soul, which the spirit as ruler does not hold within the bounds of the natural order, for the reason that it does not itself subject itself to God to be ruled. But in respect of the sense of the mind he is called sensual, who judges of God according to the phantasy of bodies, or the letter of the law, or philosophical reasoning. *Because it is spiritually examined.* The sensual man cannot understand spiritual things, because it is examined, that is, the examination and proving of those spiritual things is made only spiritually, that is, by a spiritual man, it is read personally: it is examined. Or thus: the sensual man does not understand spiritual things, because it is spiritually, that is, only through spiritual things, that it is proved that he is sensual; because he disapproves what he hears, and they are not set before him for any other cause, save that he may be examined.

*But the spiritual man.* He is such either in life or in knowledge: he is spiritual in life who, having the Spirit of the Lord for his ruler, governs his soul; but he is spiritual in knowledge who, although he sees in part and through a glass, yet savours not of him according to the images of bodies, or the letter of the law, or human philosophy, but to the spirit. Subject to God, he judges most certainly and faithfully. *spiritui. Dei subjectus*; read *spiritui Dei subjectus*, "subject to the Spirit of God" — Migne's point divides the phrase, and *Dei* is genitive with *spiritui*, not the dative *subjectus* governs *All things.* Not indeed the whole of what divine knowledge contains, but those things which suffice for righteousness and for life, that is, all things that are to be judged.

notes.text: Ye — Not the apostles, not ministers only; but all ye who are thus holy, are the salt of the earth - Are to season others. Mark ix, 50; Luke xiv, 34.

Ye are the light of the world — If ye are thus holy, you can no more be hid than the sun in the firmament: no more than a city on a mountain - Probably pointing to that on the brow of the opposite hill.
Nay, the very design of God in giving you this light was, that it might shine. Mark iv, 21; Luke viii, 16; xi, 33.
That they may see — and glorify - That is, that seeing your good works, they may be moved to love and serve God likewise.

Think not — Do not imagine, fear, hope, that I am come - Like your teachers, to destroy the law or the prophets. I am not come to destroy - The moral law, but to fulfil - To establish, illustrate, and explain its highest meaning, both by my life and doctrine.

Till all things shall be effected — Which it either requires or foretells. For the law has its effect, when the rewards are given, and the punishments annexed to it inflicted, as well as when its precepts are obeyed. Luke xvi, 17; xxi, 33.
One of the least — So accounted by men; and shall teach - Either by word or example; shall be the least - That is, shall have no part therein.
The righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees — Described in the sequel of this discourse.

glossa.text:
*You are the salt of the earth.* Here now is shown the office of the apostles, namely that they are the salt of the earth and the light of the world. This belongs especially to the apostles, who ought to be adorned with the aforesaid virtues, namely poverty and the rest, that they may be the best salt, seasoning others by doctrine and by the example of their own life. Salt, health from corruption. Whence the prophet: *I have set thee for a light of the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the ends of the earth.* 

*But if the salt,* etc. That is, if you, by whom others are to be seasoned, give way before adverse or prosperous things: by whom shall error be taken away from you, when God has chosen to raise you up for others? It is good for nothing: because (as another evangelist says) it is useful neither to the earth, which by being cast upon it it hinders from sprouting, nor to the dunghill, which it does not suffer to grow fruitful. So he who goes backward neither bears fruit himself, nor is able to till others, but is cast out of the Church, and is laughed at in these words: *This man began to build, and was not able to finish. If the salt shall lose its savor ((Luc. IV))*. That is, if through fear or through greed the teacher has let go the savor of wisdom, by whom shall his foolishness be amended? This befits the apostles alone: what follows befits all masters: *It is good for nothing any more,* etc. At the end he concludes thus concerning all: *Unless your righteousness abound,* etc.

*And be trodden upon by men.* The holy and true minister of Christ, even if he is laughed at by the wicked, cannot be trodden upon, because fixed in mind he remains in heaven.

*You are the light of the world.* Salt before light, because life before doctrine: life leads to the knowledge of truth. He who fears God does not lack knowledge.

*The light of the world.* There is another cause why they ought not to fail: because they are enlightened by Christ in word and in example: wherever they are carried among worldly men they ought to minister the light of faith and of knowledge. And as (because they are salt) they ought to drive away corruption: so also they ought to put darkness (because they are light) to flight.

*A city cannot,* etc. Because the apostles are foundations, they are fitly called a city. *Upon a mountain.* The place hints at the mountain of righteousness, which is lofty, whereby you are made public so that you may not hide yourselves. For there is no power of slipping away or of doing anything in secret; therefore rule your subjects mercifully within by counsel, and without against adversaries defend them by fighting for righteousness: which belongs to the spirit of counsel and of fortitude.

*Neither do they light a lamp.* By household examples he teaches them not to hide the light of the word committed to them. They do not light, that is, the doctrine of preaching was not given for this, that they should hide it and subject it to the servitude of the body, while they fear certain things. But let them subject their body to the ministry of God, that through the voice and the other offices of the body the light may appear more excellent than the rest. Whence it is said ((I Cor. IX)): *I chastise my body,* etc. Or, Christ lit a lamp, when he filled the earthen shell of human nature with the flame of his divinity: which he neither hid from believers, nor shut up under a bushel, that is, the measure of the law, or within the bounds of a single nation. But upon the candlestick, that is, the Church, he fastened the faith of his incarnation, where all can behold it who are in the house, that is, in the Church, or in the world. Whence he adds: *So let your light shine,* etc. *A candlestick.* As Christ is the lamp, the candlestick is the cross, upon which he was to be lifted up. The candlestick is the Church, which bears the word of the present life.

*So let your light shine,* etc. And do all these things in such a way that you do not set the end of your good work in the praises of men. *That they may see,* etc. I require works, that they may be seen, and that so the doctrine may be confirmed: and this not to your own glory.

*Do not think.* After he had exhorted them to suffer all things for the truth, and not to hide it, and to work the glory of God, he begins to teach what they are to teach. As if he were saying: What is this that thou forbiddest to be hidden, for which thou biddest all things to be suffered? is there anything against the law? *I am not come to destroy the law, but to fulfil,* either by doing what it says, or by supplying what was lacking and imperfect.

*One jot. ((BEDA.))* Here it is shown that the things which are thought least in the law are full of spiritual sacraments, and all things, etc., *as far as* because the jot signifies ten, that is, the decalogue, whose apex is the perfection of the Gospel.

*All things be fulfilled.* Let them be spiritually fulfilled, or let the imperfect be perfected, and let the things that signify be consummated, that is, by the fulfilment.


[0092D]

*He therefore that shall break,* etc. The least things are the cross of Christ and his passion, and he who is ashamed of them is least; he who confesses them is great. Or he marks the Pharisees, who let go the commandments of God for their own traditions, which are worth nothing, while they pass over even the least thing that is in the law. But morally he breaks it who does not fulfil it, but holds it as these things were given to the weak. Or he who does not understand it spiritually. To break, is not to do what one rightly understands, or not to understand what one does not distort, or to lessen the wholeness of Christ's superadding.

*He shall be called the least,* etc. In the kingdom of heaven he shall be called least who will be unworthy in it, in which there is none least but all are great.

 *But he that shall do.* He who shall not break it, and so teaches, is not least, yet not great: but he does what he teaches. *For only the doers of the law are just before God ((Rom. II))*.

*But I say to you.* When he says, I say, he struck in a great force and a deep understanding for thinking: he shows how he superadds. And he does not undo the things he had commanded before. It is even more to love enemies than not to hate them: not to covet, than not to commit adultery: not to be angry, than not to kill.

*Unless,* etc. That is, you shall fulfil not only the least precepts of the law, but also those which I add: because while the things added are done unto perfection, these too are more fully performed which were set down before unto a beginning: because he who does not look upon a woman to lust after her, neither does he commit fornication: nor does he kill who is not angry.

*Your righteousness.* He calls the righteousness of the Pharisees all those things actually commanded for the worship of God: or the mystical things of the figures, established only according to the letter.

echoes.text: Terror and dread falls on them. By the greatness of your arm they are as still as a stone— until your people pass over, Yahweh, until the people pass over who you have purchased.
echoes.note: Paul's self-description 'in weakness, in fear, and in much trembling' (v.3) draws on the stock biblical pairing of fear and trembling, programmatically stated in the Song of the Sea where 'fear and dread' and 'trembling' fall on the nations before God's power. Volume is faint and the idiom is diffuse, but it coheres with Paul's argument that the awe belongs to God's power, not human eloquence. Contested as a specific source.

echoes.text: Serve Yahweh with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
echoes.note: 'Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling' supplies the closest devotional sense of Paul's 'fear and much trembling' (v.3) as the proper posture of a servant before God's power. The verbal overlap is real in the Greek (phobos/tromos) but the phrase is formulaic, so the echo is faint and contested against the wider 'fear and trembling' tradition.

echoes.text: Thus says Yahweh, Don’t let the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, don’t let the rich man glory in his riches; but let him who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I am Yahweh who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, says Yahweh.
echoes.note: Paul's refusal of 'lofty speech or wisdom' so that faith rests 'in the power of God' (vv.1,5) extends Jeremiah's oracle that the wise must not boast in wisdom but only in knowing the LORD. The theme is carried over from 1 Corinthians 1:31, giving recurrence, but the link here is thematic rather than verbal and so faint.

echoes.text: For from of old men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither has the eye seen a God besides you, who works for him who waits for him.
echoes.note: The explicit citation formula 'as it is written' introduces v.9, 'what no eye has seen, nor ear heard...what God has prepared for those who love him,' which most closely matches Isaiah 64:4 (LXX: God acts for those who wait/love him; eye has not seen a God besides you). This is the controlling source-text, though Paul's wording is conflate and not verbatim with any extant version.

echoes.text: Daniel answered, Blessed be the name of God forever and ever; for wisdom and might are his. He changes the times and the seasons; he removes kings, and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who have understanding; he reveals the deep and secret things; he knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with him. I thank you, and praise you, you God of my fathers, who have given me wisdom and might, and have now made known […]
echoes.note: Paul's 'God's wisdom in a mystery (mysterion), hidden, foreordained before the ages' (vv.7) is steeped in Daniel's Aramaic hymn praising God 'to whom belong wisdom and might,' who 'reveals deep and hidden things.' Daniel is the Septuagintal seedbed for mysterion as divinely hidden-then-revealed knowledge, giving strong coherence with Paul's whole argument; the cluster of wisdom + mystery + revelation supplies recurrence.

echoes.text: but there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head on your bed, are these:
echoes.note: 'There is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries' is arguably the direct conceptual source for Paul's claim that God's once-hidden wisdom is now revealed (vv.7,10). The technical use of mysterion for an eschatological secret disclosed by God is distinctively Danielic, lending high coherence even without verbatim quotation.

echoes.text: “Yahweh possessed me in the beginning of his work, before his deeds of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth existed. When there were no depths, I was born, when there were no springs abounding with water. Before the mountains were settled in place, before the hills, I was born; while as yet he had not made the earth, nor the fields, nor the beginning of the dust of the world. When he established the heavens, I was […]
echoes.note: Wisdom 'foreordained before the ages for our glory' (v.7) evokes the personified Wisdom of Proverbs 8, possessed by the LORD 'at the beginning of his work, before the earth was.' The pre-cosmic, pre-temporal location of God's wisdom is the shared point; Paul transposes the Wisdom tradition christologically, so this is figural as much as verbal.

echoes.text: For she is a breath of the power of God, And a clear effluence of the glory of the Almighty; Therefore can nothing defiled find entrance into her. For she is an effulgence from everlasting light, And an unspotted mirror of the working of God, And an image of his goodness. And she, being one, has power to do all things; And remaining in herself, reneweth all things: And from generation to generation passing into holy souls She makes men friends of God and […]
echoes.note: Paul's hidden divine wisdom destined for the glory of those who love God parallels the Wisdom of Solomon's portrait of Sophia as a pure emanation of God's glory that passes into holy souls and makes them friends of God. The Second-Temple sapiential matrix (availability secure) gives strong coherence; 'for our glory' (v.7) echoes Wisdom's glory-language.

echoes.text: And with you is wisdom, which knows your works, And was present when you were making the world, And which understands what is pleasing in your eyes, And what is right according to your commandments. Send her forth out of the holy heavens, And from the throne of your glory bid her come, That being present with me she may toil with me, And that I may learn what is well-pleasing before you. For she knows all things and has understanding thereof, And in my […]
echoes.note: The motif of a wisdom present with God before the world, inaccessible to human counsel, undergirds Paul's 'wisdom of God in a mystery' that none of the rulers knew (vv.7-8). Wisdom 9 also feeds 2:16 below, giving recurrence across the chapter and strengthening the case for Paul's reliance on this prayer of Solomon.

echoes.text: Lift up your heads, you gates! Be lifted up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in. Who is the King of glory? Yahweh strong and mighty, Yahweh mighty in battle. Lift up your heads, you gates; yes, lift them up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in. Who is this King of glory? Yahweh of Armies is the King of glory! Selah.
echoes.note: 'They would not have crucified the Lord of glory' (v.8) most plausibly draws its title from the repeated 'the King of glory... the LORD of hosts, he is the King of glory.' The transfer of a divine glory-title to the crucified Christ is figural and striking; volume rests on the rare phrase 'of glory' applied to the Lord.

echoes.text: “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.
echoes.note: 'Nor did it enter into the heart of man' (v.9) closely matches Isaiah 65:17 LXX, 'the former things shall not be remembered nor come up into the heart,' suggesting Paul conflated Isaiah 64:4 with the new-creation oracle of Isaiah 65. The shared 'heart' idiom and eschatological 'what God has prepared' give this a strong claim to be part of the quotation's source matrix.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s voice is on the waters. The God of glory thunders, even Yahweh on many waters.
echoes.note: 'The God of glory thunders' offers an alternative scriptural source for Paul's 'Lord of glory' (v.8), part of the same Psalter glory-theophany vocabulary as Psalm 24. The link is faint and overlaps with the stronger Psalm 24 candidate.

echoes.text: In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple. Above him stood the seraphim. Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew. One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”
echoes.note: Isaiah's vision of the LORD high and lifted up, his glory filling the earth, lies behind the 'Lord of glory' title (v.8) as a theophanic background; rulers who 'did not know' the glory recall Isaiah's commission to a people who see but do not perceive. The connection is thematic and contested against the more verbally exact Psalm 24.

echoes.text: She is with all flesh according to his gift; And he gave her freely to those who love him.
echoes.note: Sirach 1:10, 'he supplied wisdom to those who love him,' has been proposed as a partial source for the closing phrase 'for those who love him' (v.9), since this exact clause is absent from Isaiah. The verbal tie is narrow and the dominant source remains Isaianic, so this is a contested supplementary echo.

echoes.text: he reveals the deep and secret things; he knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with him.
echoes.note: 'The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God' (v.10) coheres with Daniel's 'he reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what is in the darkness.' Within the same chapter Paul has already leaned on Daniel 2 for mystery-language (recurrence), so the depths/revelation motif here reinforces that dependence.

echoes.text: The spirit of man is Yahweh’s lamp, searching all his innermost parts.
echoes.note: 'The spirit of the man which is in him' knows 'the things of a man' (v.11) draws on Proverbs 20:27, 'the spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD, searching all the inward parts.' The shared verb 'search' and the human spirit as inner knower make this a strong conceptual source for Paul's analogy between man's spirit and God's Spirit.

echoes.text: “Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
echoes.note: 'The deep things of God' that only the Spirit can search (v.10) directly answers Zophar's challenge, 'Can you find out the deep things of God? Can you find out the limit of the Almighty?' Paul affirms what Job's friends deemed impossible, now made possible by the Spirit; the verbal tie to 'deep things of God' is close.

echoes.text: For you will not find the depth of the heart of man, and you will not perceive the things that he thinks. How will you search out God, who has made all these things, and know his mind, and comprehend his purpose? No, my kindred, don’t provoke the Lord our God to anger!
echoes.note: Judith's rebuke, 'you cannot plumb the depth of the human heart...how can you search out God who made all things, or comprehend his mind?' parallels Paul's claim that only the Spirit searches God's depths (vv.10-11) and anticipates 2:16. The Second-Temple availability is secure but the verbal overlap is loose, so the echo is faint.

echoes.text: An oracle. Yahweh’s word concerning Israel. Yahweh, who stretches out the heavens, and lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him says:
echoes.note: 'The spirit of the man which is in him' (v.11) may glance at Zechariah's description of the LORD who 'forms the spirit of man within him,' grounding the human inner spirit Paul invokes. The link is thematic and faint, overlapping with the stronger Proverbs 20:27 candidate.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: yes, he says, “It is too light a thing that you should be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give you for a light to the nations, that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.”
echoes.note: The Servant made 'a light to the nations/world' — direct background for 'you are the light of the world,' extending Israel's vocation to the disciples.

echoes.text: Every offering of your meal offering you shall season with salt; neither shall you allow the salt of the covenant of your God to be lacking from your meal offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt.
echoes.note: The 'salt of the covenant' required with every grain offering; salt as covenant-fidelity image behind 'you are the salt of the earth.'

echoes.text: All the wave offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer to Yahweh, have I given you, and your sons and your daughters with you, as a portion forever. It is a covenant of salt forever before Yahweh to you and to your seed with you.”
echoes.note: 'A covenant of salt forever' — salt symbolizing enduring covenant loyalty, the failure of which (losing savor) is the warning.

echoes.text: “I, Yahweh, have called you in righteousness, and will hold your hand, and will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations;
echoes.note: The Servant given 'as a light to the nations'; reinforces the light-to-the-world commission.

echoes.text: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory is risen on you. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you. Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.
echoes.note: Zion's light arises and nations come to its brightness; a city/light that cannot be hidden draws on this eschatological imagery.

echoes.text: It shall happen in the latter days, that the mountain of Yahweh’s house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and shall be raised above the hills; and all nations shall flow to it. Many peoples shall go and say, “Come, let’s go up to the mountain of Yahweh, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For out of Zion the law shall go out, and Yahweh’s word from Jerusalem.
echoes.note: The mountain of the LORD's house lifted up, with nations streaming to it; 'a city set on a hill cannot be hidden' evokes the eschatological Zion.

echoes.text: Those who are wise shall shine as the brightness of the expanse; and those who turn many to righteousness as the stars forever and ever.
echoes.note: The wise 'shall shine like the brightness of the firmament'; the radiance of the righteous behind 'let your light shine.'

echoes.text: Ought you not to know that Yahweh, the God of Israel, gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
echoes.note: Davidic kingship given by a 'covenant of salt'; reinforces salt's covenantal connotation.

echoes.text: But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light, that shines more and more until the perfect day.
echoes.note: The path of the righteous is like the dawning light that grows brighter; wisdom image of righteous luminance.

echoes.text: Then your light shall break out as the morning, and your healing shall spring out speedily; and your righteousness shall go before you; Yahweh’s glory shall be your rear guard.
echoes.note: When justice is done, 'your light shall break forth like the dawn'; light as visible righteous deeds (cf. 'see your good works').

echoes.text: and if you draw out your soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul: then your light shall rise in darkness, and your obscurity be as the noonday;
echoes.note: Doing good to the afflicted causes one's light to rise in darkness — coheres with light shining through good works.

echoes.text: You shall not add to the word which I command you, neither shall you take away from it, that you may keep the commandments of Yahweh your God which I command you.
echoes.note: Do not add to or take from the commandment; 'not one jot or tittle shall pass' affirms the law's inviolability in the same spirit.

echoes.text: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.”
echoes.note: 'The grass withers... but the word of our God stands forever'; heaven-and-earth-may-pass-but-the-law-endures echoes the abiding word.

echoes.text: Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look on the earth beneath; for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment; and those who dwell therein shall die in the same way: but my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.
echoes.note: 'The heavens shall vanish... but my salvation shall be forever' — direct background for 'until heaven and earth pass away, not one letter shall pass from the law.'

echoes.text: Yahweh, your word is settled in heaven forever.
echoes.note: 'Forever, O LORD, your word is settled in the heavens'; the eternal stability of Torah affirmed in v.18.

echoes.text: If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises in your midst you, and he gives you a sign or a wonder,
echoes.note: Warning against adding to or diminishing God's commands; background to the permanence of every least commandment.

echoes.text: All of your words are truth. Every one of your righteous ordinances endures forever.
echoes.note: 'Every one of your righteous ordinances endures forever'; coheres with the permanence of the least commandments.

echoes.text: This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endures for ever: all those who hold it fast are appointed to life; but such as leave it shall die.
echoes.note: 'The law... endures forever' — Second Temple affirmation of Torah's eternity behind v.18.

echoes.text: From the days of your fathers you have turned aside from my ordinances, and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you,” says Yahweh of Armies. “But you say, ‘How shall we return?’
echoes.note: Call to keep and not depart from God's statutes; resonates with not breaking the least commandments.

registers.label: Spare
lines: You are the salt of the earth.
You are the light of the world.
Share your bread; loose the bonds of the oppressed.
Then our light shall break forth like the dawn.
Let your light shine before others.
That they may give glory to God.
Come, let us worship the God who lights us.
Let our light shine. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: This is the fast God is after: not bowed heads and empty bellies, but bread broken for the hungry and the chains struck off the bound.
Let your light break forth like the dawn.
Do that, says the prophet, and your light will break out like the morning, and your healing will spring up quick.
Let your light break forth like the dawn.
You are salt, Jesus says, so do not lose your savor; you are a city on a hill that cannot be hidden.
Let your light break forth like the dawn.
So do not hide the lamp under a basket; set it high, and let the whole house fill with light.
Let your light break forth like the dawn. Thanks be to God!

lines: You are the salt of the earth, the light of the world.
Let your light break forth like the dawn.

Let your light break forth like the dawn.
Set the lamp up high, not under a basket.
Let your light break forth like the dawn.
Come, let us worship the God who lights us.
Let your light break forth like the dawn. Thanks be to God!
